errors: First draft overwrote the free edition's existing .github/workflows/einvoice-preflight-ci.yml with the paid app's CI; caught at commit review, restored, and renamed mine einvoice-pro-ci.yml.

First CI round: 5 red checks (third-party inventory, hidden U+FEFF, docker-copy false positive on a directory URL, checklist coverage for new test dirs, check_code_refs on a goals.md private-monorepo path now that apps/ exists, and the adversarial gate reading 'secrets.' + next word in a workflow comment as a secret). All fixed in one commit.

doc_friction.issue: --bets reported no free ungated item in any bet; every bet is saturated with code while none is deployed. The real blocker (private Actions start no jobs) is not a ROADMAP item, so the tool steers runs to new features instead of to the move/deploy.
Does not say that a moved app's CI file name may collide with an existing ventures/<slug> workflow (einvoice-preflight-ci.yml existed for the free edition).
workflow-escalation reads a prose comment ending 'never needs secrets.' followed by 'name:' or 'Biome' as secrets.NAME / secrets.BIOME; a comment-aware match would avoid it.

Adding any apps/ file makes goals.md's Guardrails reference to private-monorepo's apps/grants path fail; Guardrails are append-only, so the checker had to learn to skip paths named as another repository's.
A moved app needs third_party.json, hidden_unicode, checklist_coverage and publish-surface updates; none of that is listed for the next mover.

deviations.why: Default is to build the top bet's next ROADMAP item; all were claimed or gated and the products are undeployed because the private repo has no runners.
deviations.did: Took step 4 of products-to-public-repo for bet #3 (audit + move here), the prerequisite for its first deploy.
deviations.result: Moved with 0 audit blocks; tests pass locally.

deviations.why: No customer post: the work is an infrastructure move with no user-facing change yet; a post would come with the deploy.

notes: Local verification: pro 263/263, worker 9/9, checker 2231 pass/149 skip/1 env-only fail (pdfdetach -save refused by container wrapper), einvoice-site 35/35, ci_policy_check ok, risk_review blocked on nothing. packages/billing and admin-metrics copied byte-for-byte from PR #19571 so both moves merge in either order.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), fetched 2026-11-12. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads are 0.1x input except 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025x on Fable/Mythos 5.1 and 5.2. Sonnet 5.5 cache_read was 0.20 here until 2026-11-12 (quality audit round 48): records priced before then overstate Sonnet 5.5 cost.

human_equivalent.basis: audit review of 67 findings, copying and wiring CI for a 1,100-file app, local test runs

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
